## Natural history notes

A medium-sized dung beetle characterized by its shiny metallic green, coppery, reddish, or dark coloration, with males often bearing a prominent horn on the head. In Florida, it is found especially in sandy habitats such as scrub, pine flatwoods, sandhills, open woodlands, pastures, and other areas where mammal dung is available. Adults feed on dung and bury portions of it underground for their larvae, helping recycle nutrients, improve soil structure, and move organic material into the soil food web.
